title: SceneWorks memory anchor plan
$comment: sc-22514. Epic 22505 makes ONE anchor per (modelId, quant tier, backend lane) the entire measurement obligation; everything else is derived analytically by crates/sceneworks-core/src/memory_anchor.rs. This schema enforces that BY CONSTRUCTION rather than by review. The anchor set is a JSON OBJECT keyed by `<modelId>:<tier>:<backend>`, so a second measurement of the same cell is not expressible at all — not merely rejected. Every remaining axis of the grid plan it replaced is likewise inexpressible: an entry carries exactly one integer width/height/frames (no list, no range, no `cases` array), no `parameters` beyond a strategy's one exact tuple, no rung GRID (the anchor composition is FIXED per lane by the harness, mirroring `isDerivable` in scripts/extract-memory-anchors.mjs; the optional single-composition `strategy` added by sc-22734 overrides that default only where the provider CONTRACT refuses it, and is itself derived from the manifest's structural exemptions), no `expectedResult`/`negative`, and no warm-repeat, temporal or batch grouping fields. `additionalProperties: false` holds at every level, so a sweep field cannot be smuggled in under a new name.

propertyNames.$comment: `<modelId>:<tier>:<backend>` — the cell identity itself. Object keys are unique by construction, which is what makes a duplicate anchor unexpressible. The optional fourth segment (SW-F363) names one of the cell's THREE regime anchors and nothing else: `resident` (no optimization engaged; only where the base row does not already plan resident), `optimized` (every optimization the contract implements, engaged at once) and `lora` (the base composition with one community LoRA installed through LoadSpec adapters). That is the AGENTS.md two-anchor rule (lowest- and highest-memory fit, everything between derived) plus one overlay witness — a closed enum, so a regime grid is still unwritable. `validatePlan` (scripts/memory-calibration-harness.mjs) holds each regime row to its base row; crates/sceneworks-worker/src/inference_runtime.rs holds `optimized` to the contract.

strategy.$comment: sc-22734. The anchor composition is normally FIXED per lane by the harness (`ANCHOR_STRATEGY`), and this override exists for exactly one reason: a provider whose contract classifies the lane's default rung as StructurallyNotApplicable, so that `contract.validate_selection` would refuse the capture. It is still not a rung GRID — exactly one rung and one engaged set per anchor, no list of compositions — and it is not a free choice either: scripts/measure-memory-catalog.test.mjs requires the effective rung to be `resident` exactly when the model's manifest lane block declares `memoryStrategyStructuralExemptions.staged_residency`, so the override is derived from the checked-in architecture evidence rather than picked. A second, equally derived source (sc-22736): the lane's checked-in engine capability dump declares the lane default unimplemented for the provider — Candle SCAIL-2 publishes `Resident` alone and Candle LTX-2.5 publishes no `staged_residency` on any surface, `Missing` rather than structurally inapplicable — and `crates/sceneworks-worker/src/inference_runtime.rs` asks `contract.validate_selection` for every planned row on both lanes, so a row cannot plan a rung its contract refuses and cannot override to a rung the contract did not force. A REGIME row (`<cell>:resident` / `<cell>:optimized`, SW-F363) is the third source and the only one that states its composition rather than inheriting it: its strategy is required, and is bound to its regime by `validatePlan` and to the contract by the inference_runtime.rs walk.

strategyParameters.$comment: SW-F363. The ONE exact parameter tuple an engaged bounded rung executes at — each a single scalar, so a parameter sweep is still a type error. `validatePlan` requires a value for every bounded rung the strategy engages (bounded_decode: decodeTileEdge + decodeOverlap; bounded_attention: attentionChunkSize; bounded_transformer_residency: transformerWindowSize, plus an optional transformerWindowComponent; and `stageResidency: true` for staged_residency engaged by a deeper rung, because gen-core's cost order never engages staging by default — only explicit selection or this flag does) and refuses one for a rung it does not engage, which is gen-core's own `validate_selected_parameters` rule. Absent means `{}` — what every row without a bounded rung sends.

rungName.$comment: The canonical memory-ladder rung vocabulary, the same enum packages/schemas/memory-calibration.schema.json uses for a record's `strategy.rung` and `strategy.engagedRungs`.

geometry.$comment: Exactly ONE geometry per anchor. Each axis is a single integer: a list or a {min,max,step} range fails the type check, so a geometry sweep cannot be written down. This geometry is a FREE PLAN CHOICE and is deliberately NOT required to equal the geometry the packaged anchor in config/memory-anchors.json was captured at: the plan says where the NEXT capture should happen, the packaged anchor records where the LAST one did, and re-capturing a cell legitimately MOVES the packaged geometry to the planned one. Five cells disagree today on purpose (krea_2_turbo:q4:candle, flux2_dev:q4:mlx, flux2_dev:q8:mlx, ltx_2_5:bf16:mlx, ltx_2_5:q8:mlx). Nothing derives one from the other and nothing gates on their agreement — see docs/calibration-runbook.md section 2b.
